Stoczek Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Stoczek, Poland

Demolished. Jewish settlement in Stoczek likely began after Poland's partitions; by 1921, 1,221 Jews made up 74% of the town's population, most murdered at Treblinka in 1942. The cemetery, probably established in the 19th century, became a wartime execution and burial site - an estimated 200 victims of the 1942 ghetto liquidation and subsequent manhunts were buried in a mass grave here, later marked with a monument by surviving Jews after 1945. An energy line was later built through the grounds. In 1984-1985, local authorities fenced a small portion (0.10 hectares) and gathered surviving tombstones there.
